projectSummary: Two usable facts: roughly a third of specimens departed from the textbook configuration, which bounds how categorically the muscle page may describe structure; and intercostal nerve contribution was present in every stained specimen, which complicates the simple lateral-nerve-to-clavicular-head, medial-nerve-to-sternocostal-head account found in tertiary references.

publication.statusSource: Crossref REST API works record plus the Crossref/Retraction Watch CSV export, both fetched 2026-09-13

notes: The full text states the donor demographics: 40 cadavers of both sexes (22 males, 18 females), yielding 80 pectoralis major specimens; mean age 69.3 (SD 11.8) years, range 48 to 90 years. The first pass recorded donor age as not stated; it is stated, and the correction is recorded here.
A mean donor age of 69.3 years is a material applicability limitation for any claim about typical adult structure presented to lifters, and it is now stated rather than suppressed.
The attachment description in the introduction is background attributed to another source and must not be cited as this study findings.

The Sihler intramuscular staining sub-study was performed on five randomly selected muscles, not on all 80 specimens. Eighty is the gross-dissection total. Any statement about intercostal contribution to innervation rests on those five.

study.intervention: Cadaveric dissection with Sihler intramuscular nerve staining.
study.population: Forty cadavers of both sexes (22 male, 18 female) gave 80 pectoralis major specimens.

title: Anatomical Variations of the Pectoralis Major Muscle: Notes on Their Impact on Pectoral Nerve Innervation Patterns and Discussion on Their Clinical Relevance.
